Chapter 4: Questioning Assumptions and Creating New Rules
Have you ever noticed how much of our daily life is shaped by unspoken rules? Little things—like the way we stand in line, or how we fill out forms—just seem to happen because, well, that’s how it’s always been done. We rarely stop to ask, “Why does it have to be this way?”
But here’s where things get interesting. The most inspiring breakthroughs often come from people who are willing to challenge these unwritten rules. Take, for example, a student who gets frustrated by her rigid academic program. Instead of just going along with it, she gathers her courage and sits down with her professors to pitch a custom course of study. At first, they’re skeptical—you know how that goes. But her persistence and clear vision eventually win them over. She ends up creating a path for herself that opens doors she never even imagined. All because she questioned the status quo.
Or picture a junior employee at work. He spots some inefficiencies in a process that’s been around forever. Most people would just shrug and say, “That’s how we do things here.” But not him. He suggests a new way. There’s pushback at first, but as the team sees the benefits, everyone gets on board. One simple question leads to a whole new approach that makes life easier for the whole team.
The truth is, most of us don’t realize how quickly we internalize the rules around us. We get used to asking for permission, waiting for someone else to draw the lines. It’s such a common habit, we barely notice it’s there.
But think about this: some of the most exciting changes come from people who dare to challenge what everyone else takes for granted. Like a group of friends, tired of paying way too much for textbooks, who decide to launch an online platform to share resources. Sure, they hit legal and logistical roadblocks—it wasn’t easy. But their determination to find a better way pays off, and suddenly thousands of students have access to affordable materials. They discover that the world is full of problems just waiting for someone bold enough to ask, “Can we do this differently?”
So, what’s the real takeaway here? The ability to challenge assumptions isn’t just something you’re born with—it’s a skill you can build. It starts with noticing those invisible rules, then having the courage to ask, “Is there a better way?” The most meaningful changes? They usually come from the people who are brave enough to rewrite the rules, not just follow them.
